clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old woman presented with progressive isolated memory loss, specifically an impaired delayed recall (MMSE 27/30). Initial neurological examination revealed only an episodic memory deficit, with no psychiatric symptoms, seizures, or abnormal movements reported. EEG showed epileptiform discharges in the temporal lobes but no clinical seizures. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed mild pleocytosis and oligoclonal bands, and crucially, NMDAR-IgG was detected in both serum and CSF. Brain MRI showed hyperintense lesions on FLAIR and T2-weighted images in both temporal lobes. Pelvic ultrasound and MRI were normal, ruling out an ovarian teratoma. The patient was treated with IV immunoglobulins and oral prednisone, with another course of IVIG administered after 3 months.
